name: Applied Mathematics
notes: Foundational courses must be completed before acceptance into the major. AP credit may satisfy them.
Equivalent substitutions: MATH 171/172/174 for MATH 161/162/164; MATH 173 for MATH 165; MATH 141-143 for MATH 161-162.
MATH 235 may instead be satisfied by MATH 173, and should be taken early in the major.
An honors version of a course can always be substituted for the listed course.
Students choosing the physics track must ALSO complete the basic computing requirement (CSC 161 or CSC 171); students choosing the CSC track satisfy it automatically.

requirementGroups.label: Foundational mathematics
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: The following courses must be completed before acceptance into the major: MATH 161; MATH 162; MATH 164; MATH 165

requirementGroups.label: Physics or computer science pair
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: students must complete two courses from exactly one of the following subsections: PHYS 121, 122 or the honors equivalents PHYS 141, 142, 143 OR CSC 171, 172

requirementGroups.label: Basic computing requirement
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Basic computing requirement: students not choosing the computer science track above must also complete the basic computing requirement by taking either CSC 161 or 171.

requirementGroups.label: Core courses
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Core Course Requirement -- 5 courses. Students must complete the following courses: MATH 235: Linear Algebra; MATH 201: Introduction to Probability; MATH 265: Functions of a Real Variable I; MATH 280: Numerical Analysis

requirementGroups.label: Topology or complex variables
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: In addition, students must complete one of the following courses: MATH 240: Introduction to Topology; MATH 282: Introduction to Complex Variables

requirementGroups.label: Advanced courses (4)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: students must complete four 4-credit advanced courses as follows: Two advanced mathematics courses; Two additional advanced courses with substantial mathematical content. Any mathematics course numbered 200 or above (excluding courses applied to the core requirement and 500+ level) qualifies.
requirementGroups.note: The two 'substantial mathematical content' courses may come from other departments; modeled as MATH courses.

upperLevelWriting.label: Two upper-level writing courses
upperLevelWriting.sourceQuote: To satisfy the upper level writing requirement, students must pass two upper level writing courses of a certain type.
